newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU traders bid again for 277,500 tonnes soft wheat.
newsitem.headline: EU traders bid again for 277,500 tonnes soft wheat.

text.p: Grain traders bid through France on Tuesday for 277,500 tonnes of European Union soft wheat at the EU's just-increased export tax of three Ecus per tonne, cereals office ONIC said on Tuesday.
They also bid for 5,000 tonnes of durum at 10 Ecus per tonne, officials at the French authority said.
The bids came hours after the European Commission said it had rejected bids for over a million tonnes at a previous tax level of 0.5 Ecus and was raising taxes on wheat and flour.
The new bids will test the Commission's export policy again at a time when traders have accused the EU executive of failing to show consistency in its export decisions.
Traders said the Commission had appeared to leave the door ajar to exports by imposing a lower-than-expected tax of 0.5 Ecus per tonne on its daily bidding system last Thursday.

When the soaring dollar triggered over a million tonnes of bids the EU rejected them and raised the tax by 2.5 Ecus. But traders said that decision still left some EU wheat competitive, especially for November or December, and bidding could resume.

Commission sources earlier said taxes could be raised again if demand was excessive but did not say what volume the EU was willing to see going into traders' books between tenders. Most licences sought now are likely for long positions, traders said.

The mainstream tender system for grain exports is closed until August 14 but traders can bid for exports through an alternative daily channel for licences carrying fixed subsidies or taxes. Any licences issued now would be valid until end-year.
